subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes & continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@retailco.com>, Sora Patel <sora.patel@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes & continuous batching assumptions

Hi Alex / Sora — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned.

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: embed personalized recommendations and short conversational flows into RetailCo mobile app (cart + browse experiences).
- Pilot timeline: 4–6 weeks. Production ramp plan: months 3–12 with planned scale afterwards.
- Current traffic expectation: pilot ~5–10M tokens/month; production target ~200–300M tokens/month within 12 months (see questions below).
- Latency SLO: 150–300ms P95 for interactive flows; many requests are short (median 40–80 tokens).

Pricing / unit-economics discussed
- You asked for target $/1M tokens. Based on initial model selection + continuous batching, realistic target ranges are $75–$150 per 1M tokens depending on model family (open LLM vs tuned medium), quantization, and batching effectiveness.
- Example unit economics: with continuous batching + KV caching, we commonly see 20–40% effective token-cost reduction for short-turn workloads vs naive per-request execution.
- For the pilot (5–10M tokens), per-1M estimate tends to be higher due to cold-starts/less efficient batching; expect the lower-bound economics once we hit sustained traffic (~50M+/month).

Batching & concurrency assumptions (continuous batching focus)
- Continuous batching model: Redwood will aggregate requests across a short, adaptive arrival window (configurable, typically 50–150ms) to build efficient micro-batches while preserving latency SLOs.
- For streaming-heavy workloads (you indicated ~70–80% streaming), batching windows are tighter; we rely more on request coalescing and prefix caching to save token compute.
- Expected impact for your workload (median request 60 tokens, 80% streaming): ~25–35% reduction in per-token compute compared to per-request baseline.
- Concurrency guidance: pilot QPS estimate: 15–25 QPS (bursts to ~80 QPS). Production baseline: 250–400 QPS with spikes to 1k+. If you anticipate sustained spikes >500 QPS, we should discuss Reserved/Dedicated capacity.

Open questions / asks for you (helps refine pricing)
1) Can you confirm pilot vs production token volume expectations (month 1, month 6, month 12)?
2) Percent of requests that are streaming vs single-shot generation? (you mentioned ~70–80% streaming — please confirm)
3) Typical prompt + response token lengths (median and 95th percentile).
4) Any hard budget bands or target $/1M that procurement will insist on for renewal?

Next steps
- I'll loop in Aditya (SE) and Marissa (AE) for a technical deep-dive and to produce a short mutual action plan + pricing model. I attached a draft MAP and our pricing model CSV for reference.
- Proposed times for a 60-min technical deep dive: Wed Apr 7 or Thu Apr 8 (we'll include SE coverage to model batching assumptions on a short call). Please indicate which works.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

— Camila

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up: token volumes & continuous batching assumptions

Thanks Camila — very helpful summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot volumes: we expect ~6M tokens/month for the 4–6 week pilot (mostly recommendations flows).
- Production ramp: goal is 150–250M tokens/month by month 12 (we're conservative on the earlier number).
- Streaming vs single-shot: ~75% streaming, 25% single-shot.
- Token lengths: median prompt+response ~55 tokens, 95th ~320 tokens.
- Budget target: procurement wants to see a pricing band near $100–$125 per 1M tokens for the first-year commitment to evaluate TCO against our current vendor.

A couple of asks: can Aditya run a quick cost model for two scenarios — (A) hosted Redwood (usage pricing) with continuous batching enabled, and (B) Dedicated/reserved capacity for sustained production (estimate commit needed)? Also please include the expected latency P95 numbers under those scenarios given our median/95th token sizes.

We're available for the deep dive Thu Apr 8 after 11am PT.

— Alex

Appreciate the quick confirmation, Alex — that helps a lot. Looping in Aditya (SE) and Marissa (AE) to run two scenarios and validate latency implications.

Immediate plan (next 48–72h)
- Aditya: can you prepare a short cost model (spreadsheet) showing: pilot hosted cost (with expected batching uplift), 12-month projected usage cost, and a reserved capacity estimate (commit + expected per-1M after commit)? Please include assumptions for continuous batching window and expected batching efficiency for median/95th token sizes.
- Marissa: I'll coordinate procurement-facing pricing bands and put together a 1-page TCO note tied to the MAP.
- Alex / Sora: we'll send the deep-dive calendar invite for Thu Apr 8 at 11:30am PT and attach the MAP + pricing CSV for your review ahead of the call.

Technical notes for Aditya (summary of assumptions to model)
- Continuous batching window: default adaptive 50–150ms (use 100ms baseline).
- Arrival pattern: median inter-arrival ~40ms during peak; pilot peak bursts ~80 QPS; production baseline 300 QPS.
- Median tokens per request: 55 tokens; 95th: 320 tokens.
- Streaming mix: 75% streaming (partial token streaming), 25% single-shot.
- Expected batching efficiency: 25–35% token-cost reduction baseline for median requests; less benefit on 95th percentile.

Alex — we'll have the preliminary numbers by Wed EOD. If you have any additional telemetry (a short sample of QPS over a day), please send prior to the call — that would let us model continuous batching more precisely.

Thanks — Camila

Thanks Camila — noted. I'll run two scenarios and include latency P95 estimates: hosted (usage) + continuous batching, and reserved (1/3 year commit) with dedicated pools.

Quick internal note: for the numbers Alex provided, expected outcomes:
- Pilot (6M/month): hosted w/ batching -> est $/1M ≈ $125 (pilot inefficiencies considered).
- Production (150–250M/month): hosted w/ batching -> est $/1M ≈ $85–$110; reserved capacity could push to $60–$90 depending on commit level and quantization choices.
- Latency: median requests should be within the 120–180ms P95 band on current model family for streaming; 95th-tail (320 tokens) may hit 300–450ms unless we ramp worker shards or enable priority lanes.
